aspects.says: A backslash at the end of a line removes the line break and adds nothing; extra indentation of the continued line stays in the value.
basis: section:A Backslash at the End of a Line Removes the Line Break and Nothing Else

aspects.says: Every line terminator of the source, CR LF included, is LF in a text block's value.
basis: section:Line Breaks in the Source Become \n Whatever the File Uses; Only an Escape Puts \r in the Value

aspects.says: A space between a line-ending backslash and the line break is an illegal escape, reported before trailing spaces are stripped.
basis: section:A Backslash at the End of a Line Removes the Line Break and Nothing Else

aspects.says: Trailing spaces typed in a text block are stripped; a \s at the end of the line keeps them, because it is not whitespace when the stripping happens.
basis: section:\s Is a Space the Stripping Can't See, So the Spaces Before It Stay

aspects.says: translateEscapes() interprets the escapes of a literal in a string read at run time and throws IllegalArgumentException on \u.
basis: section:translateEscapes() Interprets Escapes in a String That Arrives at Run Time

aspects.says: Unicode escapes are translated before the text block is read, so \u0022\u0022\u0022 closes it.
basis: section:Unicode Escapes Are Translated Before the Compiler Sees the Text Block

aspects.says: Reproducing a text block's value from its body means translating Unicode escapes first (an escaped backslash starts none), then stripping indentation, then interpreting escapes.
basis: section:Unicode Escapes Are Translated Before the Compiler Sees the Text Block
section:translateEscapes() Interprets Escapes in a String That Arrives at Run Time

aspects.says: To write a value back as a text block, escape what would change it: backslashes, runs of three quotes, a space at the end of a line, and a carriage return.
basis: section:\s Is a Space the Stripping Can't See, So the Spaces Before It Stay
section:Line Breaks in the Source Become \n Whatever the File Uses; Only an Escape Puts \r in the Value
section:Quotes Need No Escape Until Three Stand in a Row or One Meets the Closing Delimiter
